newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey port workers in one-day protest stoppage.
newsitem.headline: Turkey port workers in one-day protest stoppage.

text.p: About 7,000 workers at 14 ports in Turkey stopped work on Wednesday in a one-day protest over the government's privatisation plan for small- and medium-sized ports, trade union officials said.
They said the protest was being staged at Istanbul, Izmir, Mersin, Derince, Bandirma, Trabzon, Hopa, Ordu, Rize, Tekirdag, Samsun, Giresun, Iskenderun and Antalya ports.
"The protest action will take 24 hours from 8 a.m. (0600 GMT)," a trade union official said.
He said the union planned more actions if the government did not give up plans to privatise ports.

Turkey last month accepted lease bids for seven small-sized and medium-sized ports as part of the privatisation plan over a 30-year period for a total of $252.3 million. A government privatisation committee is yet to approve the leases.
The one-day protest action was staged at five of the seven ports being privatised, which employ about 300 workers.
Union officials said privatisations would cause job losses, but did not say how many they expected.
Turkey's seven leading ports -- Istanbul, Mersin, Derince, Izmir, Samsun, Bandirma and Iskenderun -- belong to the State Rail Authority (TCDD) and are not in the privatisation plan.
